cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-79 requires web page generation with user-controllable input. This code serializes JavaScript functions for later reconstruction, not generating HTML output. The mechanism involves function serialization/deserialization, not HTML injection.

connection.evidence: Function values from input object are connected to placeholder generation, but no evidence shows this output reaches HTML contexts. The code explicitly escapes unsafe HTML characters before replacement operations.

diff_causality.evidence: The added line creates function placeholders during serialization. Reverting would prevent function serialization entirely, but doesn't materially change HTML generation behavior since the output is JSON with escaped characters.

security_control.required_control: HTML encoding/escaping for user-controllable content in web page generation
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-79 requires neutralization when placing user input into HTML output
existing_controls_checked: UNSAFE_CHARS_REGEXP escapes <, >, /, \u2028, \u2029 before any replacement operations
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No deficiency demonstrated - the code explicitly performs HTML character escaping before function placeholders are replaced

concrete_impact.evidence: No evidence of HTML context or script execution. The serialized output appears designed for JavaScript reconstruction, not HTML embedding.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, function values would not be serialized as placeholders, potentially breaking function serialization functionality but not materially affecting HTML generation security since the escaping mechanism remains intact.
supporting_evidence: Function values from input object are processed through serialization pipeline
Placeholder generation uses random UID to prevent pattern prediction
contradicting_evidence: Code explicitly escapes unsafe HTML characters (lines 64-66) before placeholder replacement
No evidence this serialized output is used in HTML generation contexts
Native functions are blocked from serialization (lines 83-85)
unresolved_facts: Actual usage context of serialized output (server-side vs client-side)
Whether serialized data is ever embedded in HTML pages
Downstream handling of the serialized JSON output
